summary: 74-year-old man with hypertension and a previous MI: 3 months of progressive exertional breathlessness (MRC 3), orthopnoea on 3 pillows, PND and ankle swelling.

inputs.hpi: Three months of breathlessness, getting worse: now walks slower than his wife on the level and stops for breath. Needs 3 pillows to sleep and wakes breathless at night twice a week. Both ankles swollen by the evening. No chest pain, no cough, no haemoptysis, no fever.

exam.cardiovascular: Irregular pulse? No — regular. JVP raised 4 cm. Pitting oedema to mid-shin bilaterally.

inputs.socialHistory: Ex-smoker (stopped 10 years ago). Lives with his wife.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Chronic heart failure
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Progressive exertional breathlessness with orthopnoea, PND and oedema: heart failure. NT-proBNP and echocardiography.

exacerbating: Exertion — MRC 3 slower than peers on the level

socratesAnswers.dyspnoea_exertion: MRC 3 — slower than peers on the level
socratesAnswers.orthopnoea: Orthopnoea, Paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnoea, Needs 3 pillows to sleep

mustRankTopK.note: Breathlessness frame: MRC grade → exertion, orthopnoea / PND, ankle oedema.

guideline.name: NICE NG106 — Chronic heart failure in adults: diagnosis and management
guideline.section: 1.2 Diagnosis: measure NT-proBNP in suspected heart failure; transthoracic echocardiography
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. NICE guideline NG106. London: NICE; 2018.

rationale: The breathlessness frame asks the exercise tolerance (MRC grade), orthopnoea / PND and oedema — the history that separates heart failure from lung disease. Both engines should rank heart failure.
